questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
The work function of a metal surface is $2.0\text{ eV}$. The longest wavelength of light capable of ejecting photoelectrons from this metal is closest to
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $1\text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$]
questions.explanationEn: At the threshold wavelength $\lambda_0$, $hc/\lambda_0 = \phi$. Thus $\lambda_0 = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.0 \times 10^8}{2.0 \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19}} = 6.204 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \approx 620\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following nuclei is **NMR inactive** (has nuclear spin quantum number $I = 0$)?
questions.explanationEn: Nuclei with both even mass number and even atomic number have nuclear spin $I = 0$ and are NMR inactive. $^{16}_{8}\text{O}$ has 8 protons and 8 neutrons ($I = 0$), whereas $^{13}\text{C}$, $^{19}\text{F}$, and $^{31}\text{P}$ all have $I = 1/2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: If the absolute temperature of an ideal blackbody is tripled, the wavelength $\lambda_{\max}$ corresponding to its peak spectral emissive power
questions.explanationEn: By Wien's displacement law, $\lambda_{\max} T = b$ (constant). Tripling the absolute temperature $T$ reduces $\lambda_{\max}$ by a factor of $3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The radius of the second Bohr orbit ($n = 2$) of the $\text{Be}^{3+}$ ion ($Z = 4$) in terms of the Bohr radius $a_0$ is
questions.explanationEn: For a hydrogen-like species, the radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit is $r_n = \frac{n^2}{Z}a_0$. Substituting $n = 2$ and $Z = 4$ gives $r_2 = \frac{2^2}{4}a_0 = a_0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An aqueous solution of a chromophore exhibits an absorbance of $2.0$ at $520\text{ nm}$. The percentage transmittance ($\%T$) of the solution at this wavelength is
questions.explanationEn: By definition, $A = -\log_{10} T$, so $T = 10^{-A} = 10^{-2.0} = 0.01$. Expressed as a percentage, $\%T = 0.01 \times 100\% = 1.0\%$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the pure rotational Raman spectrum of a linear rigid diatomic molecule with rotational constant $B$, the separation between the Rayleigh line and the first Stokes line, and the spacing between successive Stokes lines, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: For rotational Raman spectroscopy, $\Delta J = +2$ (Stokes branch). The shift is $|\Delta\tilde{\nu}| = F(J+2) - F(J) = B[(J+2)(J+3) - J(J+1)] = 4B(J + 3/2) = 4BJ + 6B$. For $J = 0$, the first Stokes line is displaced by $6B$ from the Rayleigh line, and successive lines ($J = 0, 1, 2, \dots$) are separated by $4B$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An excited electronic state has a lifetime of $\tau = 1.0\text{ ns}$. Using the energy–time uncertainty relation $\Delta E \cdot \tau \ge \dfrac{\hbar}{2}$, the minimum uncertainty in the frequency ($\Delta\nu$) of the emitted photon is closest to
questions.explanationEn: Since $\Delta E = h\Delta\nu \ge \frac{h}{4\pi\tau}$, we get $\Delta\nu \ge \frac{1}{4\pi\tau} = \frac{1}{4\pi \times 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s}} \approx 7.96 \times 10^7\text{ Hz} \approx 80\text{ MHz}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Assuming the force constant is unchanged upon isotopic substitution, if the harmonic vibrational frequency of $^1\text{H}^{35}\text{Cl}$ is $2990\text{ cm}^{-1}$, then the harmonic vibrational frequency of $^2\text{D}^{35}\text{Cl}$ is closest to
questions.explanationEn: Since $\tilde{\nu} \propto 1/\sqrt{\mu}$, we have $\mu_{\text{HCl}} = \frac{1 \times 35}{36} = \frac{35}{36}\text{ u}$ and $\mu_{\text{DCl}} = \frac{2 \times 35}{37} = \frac{70}{37}\text{ u}$. Hence $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{DCl}} = 2990\sqrt{\frac{35/36}{70/37}} = 2990\sqrt{\frac{37}{72}} \approx 2143\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pair(s) of quantum mechanical operators **commute** with each other?
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Position and momentum along orthogonal axes commute: $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_y] = 0$.
- **(B) True:** Total squared angular momentum commutes with any Cartesian component: $[\hat{L}^2, \hat{L}_z] = 0$.
- **(C) False:** $[\hat{L}_x, \hat{L}_y] = i\hbar \hat{L}_z \neq 0$.
- **(D) True:** Any operator commutes with a power of itself: $[\hat{p}_x, \hat{p}_x^2/(2m)] = 0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the function $f(x) = x e^{-x}$ defined on $x \in [0, \infty)$. The correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: $f(x)$ has a point of inflection at $x = 2$.
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating: $f'(x) = (1 - x)e^{-x} = 0 \implies x = 1$ (maximum, since $f''(1) = -e^{-1} < 0$), with $f(1) = e^{-1}$. Next, $f''(x) = (x - 2)e^{-x}$ changes sign at $x = 2$ (inflection point). Finally, $\lim_{x \to \infty} x e^{-x} = 0$, so (D) is false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Deviations from linearity in the Beer–Lambert law ($A = \varepsilon c l$) can arise due to
optionsEn: using polychromatic radiation instead of monochromatic radiation
chemical association or dissociation of the absorbing analyte as concentration changes
very high analyte concentrations where solute–solute electrostatic interactions alter $\varepsilon$
changing the path length $l$ of a dilute monochromatic ideal solution
questions.explanationEn: Beer–Lambert law assumes monochromatic light, dilute non-interacting species, and concentration-independent chemical equilibria. Polychromatic light (A), concentration-dependent association/dissociation (B), and high-concentration refractive/electrostatic effects (C) all cause deviations. Changing path length $l$ (D) preserves linearity $A \propto l$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct according to the Bohr model of hydrogen-like ions?
optionsEn: The orbital speed of the electron in the $n$-th orbit is proportional to $Z/n$.
The total energy of the electron in the $n$-th orbit is equal in magnitude to its kinetic energy, with opposite sign ($E_n = -K_n$).
The potential energy of the electron in the $n$-th orbit is $V_n = 2E_n$.
The orbital angular momentum of the electron is quantized as $n\hbar$.
questions.explanationEn: All four statements are exact consequences of the Bohr model and the virial theorem for a Coulomb potential: $v_n \propto Z/n$; $K_n = -E_n > 0$; $V_n = 2E_n < 0$; and $L = mvr = n\hbar$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of nodes (radial plus angular) in a $5f$ atomic orbital is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The total number of nodes in any atomic orbital is $n - 1$. For a $5f$ orbital ($n = 5, l = 3$), radial nodes $= 5 - 3 - 1 = 1$ and angular nodes $= 3$, giving $1 + 3 = 4$ total nodes.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The degeneracy of the first excited energy level ($E = \dfrac{6h^2}{8mL^2}$) of a particle in a three-dimensional cubic box of side $L$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The sum $n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 6$ is satisfied by the three permutations $(1,1,2), (1,2,1), (2,1,1)$. Hence the degeneracy is $3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The function $f(x) = x^2 - 8\ln x$ (for $x > 0$) attains its minimum at $x =$ _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Setting $f'(x) = 2x - \frac{8}{x} = 0$ gives $x^2 = 4 \implies x = 2$ (for $x > 0$). Since $f''(2) = 2 + \frac{8}{4} = 4 > 0$, $x = 2$ is a minimum.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of ways to select $3$ distinct $d$-orbitals from the $5$ available $d$-orbitals in a subshell is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The number of combinations of $3$ orbitals chosen from $5$ is $\binom{5}{3} = \frac{5!}{3!\,2!} = 10$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of chemically distinct signals observed in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of mesitylene (1,3,5-trimethylbenzene) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: By $D_{3h}$ symmetry, mesitylene has two sets of equivalent protons: the $3$ equivalent aromatic ring protons (1 singlet) and the $9$ equivalent methyl protons (1 singlet), giving $2$ signals in total.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The value of the definite integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} x^4 e^{-2x^2}\,dx$ is _______. *(round off to three decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Using the standard Gaussian integral $\int_0^\infty x^{2n} e^{-ax^2}\,dx = \frac{(2n-1)!!}{2^{n+1} a^n}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{a}}$ with $n = 2$ and $a = 2$: $I = \frac{3}{8 \cdot 2^2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} = \frac{3}{32}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} \approx 0.1175 \approx 0.118$.
